newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar closes near bottom of range.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar closes near bottom of range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar, weighed down by the Australian dollar, closed near the bottom of its range on Tuesday.
But traders said it was a dull session for the Kiwi, which was likely to continue trading in a narrow pattern unless the Aussie broke critical levels and went spiralling lower.
At 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) the Kiwi was at US$0.6939/46 from its 0.6951/58 opening and against Monday's 0.6975/85 close. The Trade-Weighted Index closed a couple of basis points below its 68.35 opening.

On Wednesday, traders will be wary of Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's testimony to parliament's Finance and Expenditure Committee but they do not expect him to alter the line he took last week at the bank's six monthly forecasts.
The bank assumed a mix of a TWI at 68 and 90-day bank bills at 7.5 percent.
Dealers said there was little interest in the Kiwi, with small longs continuing to unwind being the main feature.
One said his view at these levels was neutral, with buyers lined up around 0.6935 and sellers at 0.6960.
The Australian dollar was seen on critical support at US$0.7900/05.

"If the Aussie breaks through 0.7880 then the Kiwi is going to break through support at 35-40. And if that happens we'd probably go fairly quickly down to the 0.6890 area but there would be a lot of exporter interest there," said another dealer. "Really the next Kiwi support level is around the 0.6885 level. Below 69 cents the exporters would do reasonable amounts." -- Simon Louisson 64 4 4714 276
